title: mosaic-objective-sprint-scratch - Rina Kaur
body:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for the next two-week mosaic sprint. This is a personal, informal doc - mostly stream-of-consciousness + checkpoints I want to carry between weekly check-ins. Not a polished PRD, just signal + decisions log.

Sprint theme: Reduce token-cost variance & stabilize latency for our mid-tail workloads (50-200 tokens). Personal outcome: move two levers that reduce average per-request cost by 8-12% without increasing 95th pct latency more than 10ms.

Leading indicators to watch (tracked daily):
- % of requests hitting prefix cache (goal +5pp)
- avg tokens per session (target down 3%)
- batching throughput (tokens/sec net for the batcher)
- quantized runtime errors (count)
- infra cost estimate delta (rough $/k request)

Concrete experiments (prioritized):
1) Prefix cache TTL tuning (timebox: 3 days)
   - hypothesis: lowering TTL from 120s -> 60s for short-lived sessions increases cache hit for our mid-tail by ~4% with negligible miss penalty.
   - success metric: cache_hit_rate_up >= 3% AND 95th latency delta <= +10ms.
   - steps: config change -> smoke test -> A/B on low-traffic route -> rollback plan.
   - risks: increased cache churn causing CPU overhead. Monitor eviction_rate.

2) Adaptive mini-batching (timebox: 5 days)
   - idea: add a soft threshold that prefers packing requests with similar max-length to reduce padding tokens inside batches.
   - hypothesis: reduces tokens emitted to runtime by 6-10% for mixed-length workloads.
   - success metric: effective_token_reduction >= 5% and end-user p50 latency <= baseline.
   - blockers: needs minor runtime touch + telemetry event (batch_shape) instrumented.

3) Quick quantization rollout for dev routes (timebox: 4 days)
   - try 4-bit activation quantization on a small dev model. Track quality degradation via sampling of live prompts.
   - metric: automated quality score (BLEU-ish proxy) drop < 1.5% and cost reduction > 10%.

Weekly check-in format (what I actually say in standup):
- yesterday: TTL tuning config + smoke tests ran, eviction spike on node B, investigating
- today: finish eviction mitigation (pin hot prefixes), start adaptive-batcher prototype
- blockers: telemetry for batch_shape not yet in prometheus -> need infra help (Jae)
- ask: can Maya allocate 2 hours this week to write the sampling harness for quality checks?

Retro notes (from last sprint):
- shipped micro-cache change but didn't track user-quality metric; need to bake sampling earlier
- learned: small config flips can have noisy short-term signals; longer warm windows help
- action: add a gated rollout that requires 48h of steady-state metrics before broadening.

Personal cadence + micro-OKR mapping:
- Objective: Make mid-tail inference 10% cheaper without regressions
  - KR1: +5% cache hit on mid-tail routes (owner: me)
  - KR2: introduce batching heuristic and measure >=5% token reduction (owner: me + Jae)
  - KR3: deploy quantized dev variant and collect quality samples (owner: me + Maya)

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep check-ins small and specific; "did you reduce cost? by how much?" beats long design notes.
- When in doubt, snapshot current metrics before change (use /metrics/snapshot endpoint).
- If eviction_rate climbs, consider moving heavy prefixes to hot-cache group instead of bumping global memory.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the acceptable quality proxy threshold for a dev quantized model? (ask Maya)
- Can we wire batch_shape telemetry to a low-cardinality metric to avoid prometheus costs? (ask infra)
- Find a way to correlate sample prompts with customer buckets for regressions.

Decision log (short):
- 2026-02-20: TTL change staged to canary (route: /gen/small).
- 2026-02-23: Reverted TTL change after eviction spike on node B; plan: pin hot prefixes and retry.
- 2026-03-02: Decided to prototype adaptive mini-batching rather than full scheduler rewrite.

Jot list (things I might turn into tickets):
- Add batch_shape histogram + example request payload sampler (JIRA-822?)
- Small runtime flag to prefer similar-length packing (feature flag + tests)
- Sampling harness for quantization quality (needs Maya)

End-of-sprint thoughts:
- Keep this doc alive for the next sprint; strip items that turned into tickets and add measurement links.
- Short, frequent experiments with clear rollbacks work better for infra risk.

---
If I come back in 2 weeks, I want a tiny table: experiment | date started | primary metric delta | go/no-go. For now this is messy, which is fine.
